results.title: Chief factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A / B$ is a chief factor of $G$ if $A$ and $B$ are normal in $G$, $B < A$, and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $B \le N \le A$ equals $B$ or $A$.

results.title: Groups of Fitting height at most $h$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $h$, a group $G$ has Fitting height (nilpotent length) at most $h$ if there are normal subgroups $1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_h = G$ of $G$ such that for every $i < h$ some term of the lower central series of $G_{i+1}$ lies in $G_i$, that is, $G_{i+1} / G_i$ is nilpotent.

results.title: Composition factors via subnormal subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $S$ is a composition factor of a group $K$ if $S$ is simple and some subnormal subgroup $H$ of $K$ has a surjective homomorphism onto $S$.

results.title: Conjugacy separable groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is conjugacy separable if any two elements $x, y \in G$ whose images are conjugate in every quotient $G / N$ by a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index (that is, $g x g^{-1} y^{-1} \in N$ for some $g \in G$) are conjugate in $G$.

results.title: Residually finite $p$-groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is residually a finite $p$-group if every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ lies outside some normal subgroup of $G$ whose index is $p^k$ for some $k \ge 0$, where an infinite index counts as $0$.

results.title: Restricted wreath product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $A$ and $B$, let $A \wr_r B = A^B \rtimes B$ be the regular (unrestricted) wreath product, where $A^B$ is the group of all functions $f : B \to A$ and $b \in B$ acts on it by $(b \cdot f)(x) = f(b^{-1} x)$. The restricted wreath product $A \wr B$ is the subgroup of $A \wr_r B$ generated by the elements $(f, b)$ whose function part $f$ has finite support, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for only finitely many…

results.title: Partitions of the primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers is a partition of the primes if every $\sigma_i$ is a nonempty set of primes, $\sigma_i$ and $\sigma_j$ are disjoint whenever $i \ne j$, and every prime lies in some $\sigma_i$.

results.title: $\sigma$-primary numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a natural number $n$ is $\sigma$-primary if there is an index $i$ such that every prime divisor of $n$ lies in $\sigma_i$. For $n = 0$ this means that some $\sigma_i$ contains every prime.

results.title: $\sigma$-subnormal subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$ if there is a chain of subgroups $A = A_0 \le A_1 \le \cdots \le A_n = G$ such that for every $i < n$ either $A_i$ is normal in $A_{i+1}$, or the index in $A_{i+1}$ of the normal core of $A_i$ in $A_{i+1}$ is $\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).

results.title: $\sigma$-nilpotent groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-nilpotent if it is the internal direct product of finitely many normal subgroups $H_1, \dots, H_t$ whose orders are $\sigma$-primary (the order of an infinite subgroup counts as $0$): the $H_k$ generate $G$, and each $H_k$ meets the subgroup generated by the others trivially.

results.title: $\sigma$-soluble groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-soluble if for every chief factor $A / B$ of $G$ the index $|A : B|$ is $\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).

results.title: Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question (Kourovka 19.84)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, every finite group $G$ and every subgroup $A$ of $G$, if $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, then $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.

results.title: A counterexample to Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 19.84 is false: there are a partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $A$ of $G$ such that $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, but $A$ is not $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.

results.title: Kourovka 20.30: the order of a perfect centreless group and its largest conjugacy class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every finite group $G$ that is perfect ($[G, G] = G$) and has trivial centre contains an element $x$ with $|G| \le |x^G|^2$, where $x^G$ is the conjugacy class of $x$. Equivalently, $|G| \le n^2$, where $n$ is the largest size of a conjugacy class of $G$.

results.title: Perfect centreless groups need not have order at most the square of the largest class size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that every finite group $G$ that is perfect ($[G, G] = G$) and has trivial centre contains an element $x$ with $|G| \le |x^G|^2$, where $x^G$ is the conjugacy class of $x$. That is, some perfect centreless finite group $G$ satisfies $|G| > n^2$, where $n$ is the largest size of a conjugacy class of $G$.

results.title: The POND condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the POND condition when no odd number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every odd part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the odd parts are not distinct.

results.title: The PEND condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the PEND condition when no even number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every even part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the even parts are not distinct.

results.title: Number of POND partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ that are POND, that is, in which every odd part that occurs has multiplicity at least $2$ (OEIS A265256).

results.title: The PEND partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ is the number of PEND partitions of $n$: partitions of $n$ in which every even part that occurs appears at least twice (OEIS A265254).

results.title: The number of POND partitions of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $\mathrm{pond}(0)$ of POND partitions of $0$ equals $1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty partition, and it is POND.

results.title: PEND partitions of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number of PEND partitions of $0$ is $1$, that is, $\mathrm{pend}(0) = 1$.

results.title: Examples of POND and PEND parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multisets of parts $\{1, 1\}$ and $\{2\}$ satisfy the POND condition, while $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 1\}$ do not; the multisets $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 2\}$ satisfy the PEND condition, while $\{2\}$ and $\{2, 4\}$ do not.

results.title: Congruences modulo 2, 3 and 4 for POND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}$, $\mathrm{pond}(27n + 26) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ and $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{4}$.

results.title: Congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions of 27n + 19
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(27n + 19) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

results.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for POND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(27n + 17) \equiv \mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \pmod{3}$.

results.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(27n + 10) \equiv \mathrm{pend}(3n + 1) \pmod{3}$.

results.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for POND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$, $\mathrm{pond}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (23 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} + 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

results.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for PEND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$, $\mathrm{pend}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (17 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} - 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

results.title: Prime-power congruence for powers of Euler products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $j, k, m \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and let $f_m = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{mi})$. Then for every natural number $n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_m^{p^j k}$ is congruent modulo $p^j$ to the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_{pm}^{p^{j-1} k}$.

results.title: Generating function for POND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ be the number of POND partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series in $q$, $f_2^2 f_3 f_{12} \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2$. This is the identity $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2 / (f_2^2 f_3 f_{12})$ with the denominator cleared.

results.title: Generating function for PEND partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series in $q$, $f_1 f_4 f_6 \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12}$. This is the identity $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12} / (f_1 f_4 f_6)$ with the denominator cleared.

results.title: Hypergraph
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A hypergraph on a type $V$ of vertices is a set of subsets of $V$; its elements are the edges of the hypergraph. Edges may be empty, and no finiteness condition is imposed.

results.title: Edge coloring of a hypergraph
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypergraph on a vertex type $V$ and let $\alpha$ be a type. An $\alpha$-coloring of $\mathcal{H}$ is a map $c$ from the set of edges of $\mathcal{H}$ to $\alpha$ such that $c(e_1) \ne c(e_2)$ for any two distinct edges $e_1$ and $e_2$ of $\mathcal{H}$ that have a vertex in common.

results.title: Linear hypergraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is linear if any two distinct edges of $\mathcal{H}$ have at most one vertex in common.

results.title: Chromatic index of a hypergraph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The chromatic index of a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is the least natural number $n$ such that $\mathcal{H}$ has a coloring with colors in $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.

results.title: Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for sufficiently many vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sufficiently large natural number $n$, every linear hypergraph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ has chromatic index at most $n$.

results.title: Naive string matcher
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern and $t = t_0 \cdots t_{n-1}$ a text over an alphabet with a Boolean equality test. If $m \le n$, the naive matcher handles the shifts $s = 0, 1, \dots, n - m$ in turn: it compares $p_i$ with $t_{s+i}$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots$ until a comparison fails or all $m$ symbols are compared, and it reports $s$ if no comparison failed. It returns the reported shifts in the order found,…

results.title: Output of naive matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a pattern of length $m$ and $t$ a text of length $n$. If $m \le n$, the list of shifts reported by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is the increasing list of all $s \in \{0, \dots, n - m\}$ such that $p$ is a prefix of the suffix of $t$ starting at the zero-based position $s$, with symbols compared by the Boolean equality of the alphabet. If $m > n$, the list is empty.

results.title: Correctness of naive string matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality agrees with equality, and write $|t|$ for the length of a list $t$. For every pattern $p$ and text $t$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $s$, the naive matcher run on $p$ and $t$ reports the shift $s$ if and only if $p$ matches $t$ at $s$, that is, $s \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the suffix of $t$ obtained by dropping its first $s$ symbols.

results.title: Naive matching reports shifts in increasing order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every pattern $p$ and text $t$, the list of shifts reported by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is strictly increasing; in particular, no shift is reported twice.

results.title: Exact comparison count of naive matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern and $t = t_0 \cdots t_{n-1}$ a text. If $m \le n$, the number of symbol comparisons performed by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is

results.title: Upper bound on the comparisons of naive matching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a pattern of length $m$ and a text of length $n$, the naive matcher performs at most $(n - m + 1) \cdot m$ symbol comparisons if $m \le n$, and no comparisons if $m > n$.

results.title: Naive matching on a repeated symbol reports every shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality is reflexive, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $m \le n$ be natural numbers. On the pattern consisting of $m$ copies of $x$ and the text consisting of $n$ copies of $x$, the naive matcher reports exactly the shifts $0, 1, \dots, n - m$ in increasing order, so all overlapping occurrences are reported.

results.title: Comparison count of naive matching on a repeated symbol
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality is reflexive, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $m \le n$ be natural numbers. On the pattern consisting of $m$ copies of $x$ and the text consisting of $n$ copies of $x$, the naive matcher performs exactly $(n - m + 1) \cdot m$ symbol comparisons.

results.title: Naive matching with the empty pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every text $t$ of length $n$, the naive matcher run on the empty pattern and $t$ reports exactly the shifts $0, 1, \dots, n$ in increasing order and performs no symbol comparisons.

results.title: Naive matching with a pattern longer than the text
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the pattern $p$ is longer than the text $t$, then the naive matcher run on $p$ and $t$ reports no shifts and performs no symbol comparisons.
